name: Ticket
description: Plan with pi, approve it (or send it back with a comment), implement with claude, verify with the project's test command, then approve the PR and a deterministic publish stage pushes and opens it.

plan.title: Plan
plan.instructions:
You are the planning stage. Inspect the project's repos (in your working directory). Do not change any files.

Reply with a concise implementation plan in markdown. The FIRST line of your reply must be exactly `BRANCH: <branch>` — the git branch this work will live on, named by these rules, first match wins:
1. If the task names a ticket or issue key (e.g. `ENG-1234`) or an explicit branch, use it: `<KEY>-<slug>` or the named branch verbatim.
2. Else, if the brief's "# Project" section lists a branch prefix, use `<prefix>/<slug>`.
3. Else use `ticket/<slug>`.
`<slug>` is a short kebab-case topic from the task.

If the brief carries "# Feedback from Chad" (a re-plan), revise the previous plan to address every point.

approve.title: Approve plan
approve.instructions: Review the plan and its branch name. Approve it to implement, send it back with a comment to revise, or reject to end the run.

next.when: Revise (add a comment for the planner)

implement.title: Implement
implement.instructions:
You are the implementation stage. Follow the approved plan from the earlier stage exactly: create its branch (the plan's BRANCH line), make the changes, and commit with clear messages. Do not push.

For visual changes, serve your work before finishing: call start_preview (the project's saved setup defaults dir/command/port; first run on a setup-less project, save one with save_preview_setup) and confirm the app actually comes up at the preview URL. Never hand-build a QA environment — no apt installs, no ad-hoc databases, no background servers outside a preview. When driving agent-browser, follow its installed skill (~/.claude/skills/agent-browser) — snapshot-and-refs, batch sequences, one command per line.

verify.title: Verify
verify.instructions: You are the QA stage. Verify the work on the branch named in the earlier plan (its BRANCH line). Run the project's test command from the brief's "# Project" section — or, when it is not set, the repo's own test script, saying which you ran. At minimum confirm the planned changes are present and committed. For visual changes, review the screenshots the implementer attached (listed under their stage in this brief) and make ONE live spot-check against the preview — start_preview is idempotent per sandbox/directory/port, so calling it returns the same preview they started. Your job is the diff, the test gate, and that spot-check: do NOT re-validate the environment a prior stage described — a cold stop_preview → start_preview on the saved setup IS the environment test. Report what you actually saw, never a claim you did not check. When driving agent-browser, follow its installed skill: snapshot-and-refs, and batch command sequences instead of one command per call. When the work is correct, declare the PR with the propose_pr tool (repo = the repo's directory name, head = that branch, title = one line summarizing the change), then transition to the approval gate; if it needs fixes, transition back to implement and explain exactly what is wrong.

next.when: The work is correct and committed (PR declared)

pr-approve.title: Approve PR
pr-approve.instructions: The PR proposal recorded by the previous stage is shown on the card (branch, commits, diffstat). Approve it to push the branch and open the PR, send it back with a comment for changes, or reject to end the run.

next.when: Request changes (add a comment for the implementer)

publish.title: Publish
publish.instructions: Deterministic: pushes the approved branch and opens the approved PR.
